scope: Manual comparison of ten remaining interfaces of aos-2024-v52-i04-p1845, retaining the registered source's smoothness, architecture, conditional-law and lower-bound estimator conventions.

rows.query: Searched Holder smoothness and partial-derivative interfaces; inspected HolderOnWith, iterated Frechet derivatives and finite-order differentiability against Definition 2.1.
rows.result: Holder continuity of scalar derivative coordinates is available, but equivalence with the exact multi-index derivative condition and its constant needs a construction and proof.
rows.gap: Construct the order-r partial derivatives and impose the source's global Euclidean Holder bound with constant C, preserving r=0 and the endpoint s=1.

comparisons.D5: Write beta=r+s with r a nonnegative integer and 0<s<=1; when beta is an integer this uses r=beta-1,s=1 rather than s=0. HolderOnWith on the whole real Euclidean domain supplies exactly the scalar distance inequality for each chosen rth partial derivative, after translating positive real C and s into nonnegative parameters. For r=0 the derivative is f itself. iteratedFDeriv can supply derivative coordinates by evaluation on repeated coordinate vectors only with the needed differentiability and identification proofs; its totalized fderiv construction does not assert existence of source partials. A bound on the whole multilinear derivative norm is not automatically the same constant as separate coordinate bounds. No global supremum bounds on f or lower derivatives are part of this definition. Preserve the prose numerator partial f and the display partial^r f as recorded; the unit-cube example later in the paper needs its own extension/domain convention.

rows.query: Searched hierarchical composition and neural-network function classes; inspected derivative and Holder building blocks and compared the recursive quantifiers of Definition 2.2.
rows.result: The component smoothness predicates have analytic ingredients, but the depth-indexed composition class is not an inspected pre-existing library interface.
rows.gap: Define the recursive composition class with arbitrary coordinate reuse, its bounded smoothness/arity index set and locally quantified positive smoothness constants.

comparisons.D6: At depth one choose (beta,t) in P, a positive C, a (beta,C)-smooth g:R^t->R and any map pi:[t]->[d]. pi need not be injective, so repeated coordinates are permitted. At depth l>1 choose t members of H(d,l-1,P) and compose them with such a g; this internal recursion is not a cyclic external dependency. P is a subset of [1,infinity) times positive integers with bounded max(beta,t), and d,l are positive. The same bounded P is used through recursion, but C is quantified inside the formulas and is not declared a common global bound across the whole class. Holder and derivative primitives do not themselves encode the recursive representation or prove neural approximation. In particular the later proposition's dependence on C cannot silently strengthen this class.

rows.query: Searched neural-network architecture interfaces; inspected integer ceilings and logarithms against (3.15) and the frozen Proposition 3.4 constant context.
rows.result: The logarithmic ceiling expressions can be formed, but network-size typing and the source approximation constants require their own specification.
rows.gap: Construct the enlarged integer architecture from c3 ceil(L log L) and c4 ceil(N log N), retaining the proposition's parameter dependence and constant-scope issue.

comparisons.D21: The architecture is L-bar=c3 ceil(L log L), N-bar=c4 ceil(N log N) for the output-truncated F_n(d,L-bar,N-bar,M). The referenced proposition uses L,N>=3 and constants depending only on composition depth, sup_P max(beta,t), and C. It supplies existential constants, not numerical values. Int.ceil returns an integer, but multiplication by a merely stated positive constant does not automatically produce a natural network dimension; an admissible size/rounding convention or integer choice for constants needs justification rather than an extra silent ceiling. The source class quantifies C internally while the proposition depends on C, and that uniformity issue remains. Preserve the network convention of L-bar hidden ReLU stages and L-bar+1 affine maps, not an altered layer count or parameter bound.

rows.query: Inspected minimum predicates and compact attainment hypotheses; compared the bounded index set P with the selected smoothness-to-arity minimizer in (2.6).
rows.result: A selected minimum ratio can be specified, but boundedness of P alone does not establish the nonempty compact domain needed by the inspected attainment theorem.
rows.gap: Supply an attained minimizing pair in P and a tie convention, then define gamma-star as its beta-to-arity ratio.

comparisons.D7: Require the selected (beta-star,d-star) to belong to P as well as satisfy IsMinOn of (beta,t)->beta/t, since IsMinOn itself does not require membership. Positive t makes each ratio meaningful. The source bounds beta and t but does not require nonempty or closed P; for example a bounded open interval of beta with fixed t can have an unattained infimum. IsCompact.exists_isMinOn therefore needs additional hypotheses not supplied by that bound. Do not replace a chosen argmin pair by a bare infimum or silently resolve ties. The scalar minimizing value may be common among ties while beta-star and d-star need not be unique. This least component ratio differs from the later minimax-risk definition of intrinsic smoothness.

rows.query: Inspected uniform-law normalization and conditional expectation on the sigma-algebra generated by X; compared the lower-bound experiment family with its standing source conventions.
rows.result: Uniform cube design and conditional mean/moment constraints have direct law and expectation ingredients, but the complete experiment family must be assembled with genuine integrability.
rows.gap: Construct the uniform-design experiment family with conditional mean zero and pth absolute moment at most one, preserving the arbitrary supplied regression class.

comparisons.D18: U(d,p,F) consists of triples (X,f0,epsilon) with X uniform on [0,1]^d, f0 in F, E[epsilon|X]=0 and E[|epsilon|^p|X]<=1. IsUniform uses normalized restricted reference volume, not a discrete uniform PMF; the real cube has finite positive volume. condExp on the sigma-algebra generated by X gives the conditional constraints almost surely after measurability, integrability and sub-sigma-algebra conditions. Its zero fallback for a nonintegrable input must not certify a moment bound. In the theorem the class is specialized to F0 and Section 4 has its bounded-regression convention; the family itself does not impose Holder derivative smoothness or the hierarchical class. Conditional mean zero is not design-noise independence, and the lower-bound laws need not be Gaussian or symmetric. The standing iid sampling then defines repeated observations from each such experiment.

rows.query: Inspected products of coordinate intervals and integer floors; compared grid size, tolerance and terminal-cell indicator in the sub-hypercube definition (4.8).
rows.result: Finite products of closed coordinate intervals implement the regions once the positive integer grid is established, with gaps removed only from nonterminal cells.
rows.gap: Assemble each product region with its exact terminal-index exception and prove the grid and tolerance domains valid.

comparisons.D20: K=floor(N^(1/d))^2 floor(L^(1/d))^2 for positive integer N,L and positive dimension, and alpha ranges over {1,...,K}^d. Q_alpha(Delta) uses closed coordinate intervals [(alpha_i-1)/K,alpha_i/K-1_{alpha_i<K} Delta] for every coordinate. Set.pi of Set.Icc expresses those simultaneous inequalities, with the all-coordinate interpretation recorded separately from the source display's abbreviated quantifier. The final coordinate cell has no subtraction and reaches 1; this is not a half-open partition and the nonterminal cells have one-sided gaps. Delta lies in (0,1/(3K)] and epsilon in (0,1); the precision parameter and arbitrary y_alpha in [0,1] do not alter Q. Real roots and floors require positive-domain typing and a justified positive natural K. No global bound on the fitted network away from these regions follows from this set definition.

rows.query: Inspected measurable-function and closed-interval predicates; compared the source's pointwise uniform bound with essential L-infinity bounds and continuous bounded-function spaces.
rows.result: Measurable real functions on the cube with every value in [-M,M] express the comparison class without imposing continuity or passing to almost-everywhere equivalence classes.
rows.gap: Assemble the bounded measurable comparison class using the same M as Condition 1 and the source's pointwise supremum convention.

comparisons.D14: Theta includes all measurable f:[0,1]^d->R with sup over cube points of |f(x)|<=M, where M>=1 is the same bound as Condition 1. On the nonempty cube this can be expressed directly by Measurable f and f(x) in [-M,M] for every x, with the usual supremum equivalence on bounded functions. MemLp infinity supplies only an essential bound and would discard exceptional point values; a bounded continuous-function structure would add continuity. Neither change is appropriate. The class is also broader than the neural-network class, and its functions retain representatives for subsequent empirical evaluation at observed covariates.

rows.query: Inspected constrained minimum and population integral predicates; searched population Huber minimizers and compared mean-zero and symmetric-noise interpretations.
rows.result: A selected population-risk minimizer is expressible, but existence, representative choice and equality with the regression mean are not supplied by generic minimization.
rows.gap: Construct a bounded measurable population Huber minimizer with a valid risk and selection convention; equality with f0 requires further noise assumptions.

comparisons.D15: The definition selects f0,tau in argmin over Theta of R_tau, so membership in the measurable bounded class must accompany IsMinOn. It is not minimization over the network class or the empirical sample. Finite positive tau gives a loss with linear tails, allowing finite risk under the first-moment setting and bounded functions once proved. At tau=infinity the loss is half squared error, and finite first moment alone does not give finite population risk; a real integral's nonintegrable zero fallback cannot stand for infinite loss. An extended-risk formulation or the appropriate second-moment domain is required there. Mean-zero asymmetric noise can shift the Huber minimizer away from f0; uniqueness, measurable selection and representative choices are not established by IsMinOn. The later empirical comparison to f0,tau makes those representative choices material.

rows.query: Searched Huber and neural approximate-minimizer interfaces; inspected real infimum requirements and compared both disjunctive eligibility branches in (4.3).
rows.result: Infimum inequalities support the objective comparisons, but the two-branch neural estimator set and its statistical lower-bound interpretation require explicit construction.
rows.gap: Construct the lower-bound estimator set with its exact min-condition OR n^-100 condition, keeping the selected population minimizer and universal c9 on their source scales.

comparisons.D19: Candidates belong to F_n(d,L-bar,N-bar,1). The first branch requires empirical risk at most min{empirical risk of f0,tau, inf over that network class of empirical risk+c9 delta^2}; this is BOTH comparisons, not a choice between them. The second branch is OR empirical risk at most the same infimum+n^-100. Preserve this union and the arbitrary robustification parameter rather than replacing it with the upper-bound set S_n,tau(delta). c9 is universal and independent of architecture, n and tau. Infimum order facts require a nonempty class and a lower-bounded real objective range, obtainable for valid finite sample losses and an established zero network; they do not assume exact minimizer attainment. Population f0,tau need not be a member of the network class. Huber at infinity has the source's half-squared-loss normalization, so numeric tolerances cannot be transferred unchanged to (2.3). The lower theorem asserts existence of a bad eligible estimator, not that every eligible member is bad.

rows.query: Inspected regular conditional laws, equal-law predicates and absolute first moments; compared the every-x symmetric-noise condition with almost-everywhere conditional-law guarantees.
rows.result: Symmetry can be specified by invariance of each conditional law under negation, but a pointwise version satisfying the uniform first-moment bound must be supplied.
rows.gap: Specify a conditional noise-law version symmetric at every cube point with uniformly bounded first absolute moment, without adding a second-moment assumption.

comparisons.D4: For every x in the cube the conditional law of epsilon given X=x is symmetric about zero and its integral of |epsilon| is at most v1>0. At a fixed conditional law, IdentDistrib of the identity and negation expresses symmetry once their measurability is established. condDistrib supplies a regular conditional kernel for real noise, but the connection to conditioning and uniqueness is almost everywhere in X; it does not certify these every-x properties of an arbitrary version. A version satisfying them must be stipulated or constructed, including values at null covariates. Finite absolute first moments justify actual integrals and conditional means; nonintegrable zero fallback is not a bound. Neither finite variance nor independence of the conditional law from x follows, and Theorem 3.7's separate c1 parameter-scope issue cannot be resolved by silently imposing Condition 2 at order two.
